title: A Train for Heavy Loads

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: How can one engine move several loaded train cars?
storyBibleReview.progression: Follow one illustrative short freight train from separate loaded cars, through their couplers and powered locomotive, along a track to unloading.
storyBibleReview.synthesis: The engine provides power while connected cars carry the load together.

scienceSources.title: Association of American Railroads: Freight Rail Operations 101
scienceSources.evidence: Steel wheelsets support railcars on rails; couplers are strong links joining cars. This example has one locomotive and three cars, not a claim that every train uses one engine.

scienceSources.title: Association of American Railroads: Freight Rail Facts
scienceSources.evidence: A locomotive powers a train and freight cars carry goods.

setting: A short contemporary freight journey between two warehouses. No public access to tracks. Unbranded blue diesel-electric locomotive, followed by red, yellow and green enclosed boxcars in that fixed order. Adult railway workers have orange safety vests, blue trousers and hard hats.
props: Exactly three boxcars in red/yellow/green order
Gray steel couplers between all vehicles
Wooden crates secured inside the cars
coverBrief: Side view of the blue locomotive pulling its three connected freight cars past a warehouse; true wheels on rails, visibly closed couplers, no letters or logos.

pages.text:
These heavy boxes need a ride.
They fill three train cars.
pages.imageBrief: Warehouse loading bay. Three open boxcars contain securely stacked wooden crates; fixed red/yellow/green order. Blue locomotive waits ahead.
pages.imageAlt: Warehouse loading bay. Three open boxcars contain securely stacked wooden crates; fixed red/yellow/green order. Blue locomotive waits ahead.
pages.pageDescription: Warehouse loading bay. Three open boxcars contain securely stacked wooden crates; fixed red/yellow/green order. Blue locomotive waits ahead.
pages.state: Three loaded cars; doors open; locomotive not moving.

pages.text:
Each car has wheels.
The wheels rest on two rails.
pages.imageBrief: Low close view of a red boxcar bogie; paired steel wheels sit correctly on two parallel rails, with crate-filled car above.
pages.imageAlt: Low close view of a red boxcar bogie; paired steel wheels sit correctly on two parallel rails, with crate-filled car above.
pages.pageDescription: Low close view of a red boxcar bogie; paired steel wheels sit correctly on two parallel rails, with crate-filled car above.
pages.state: Same red car; steel wheels and track geometry clear.

pages.text:
Strong metal links join the cars.
These links are called couplers.
pages.imageBrief: Close view between red and yellow boxcars shows one correctly joined knuckle-coupler pair and separate brake hose.
pages.imageAlt: Close view between red and yellow boxcars shows one correctly joined knuckle-coupler pair and separate brake hose.
pages.pageDescription: Close view between red and yellow boxcars shows one correctly joined knuckle-coupler pair and separate brake hose.
pages.state: One actual coupling, no human hand near it.

pages.text:
An engine joins the front car.
It gives this train its power.
pages.imageBrief: Blue locomotive is coupled to the red first car; yellow and green follow. All freight doors are now shut.
pages.imageAlt: Blue locomotive is coupled to the red first car; yellow and green follow. All freight doors are now shut.
pages.pageDescription: Blue locomotive is coupled to the red first car; yellow and green follow. All freight doors are now shut.
pages.state: All four vehicles connected in fixed order; loading complete.

pages.text:
The engine pulls.
The linked cars move along the track.
pages.imageBrief: Whole short train begins rolling away from warehouse; rails curve gently ahead and all wheelsets stay on them.
pages.imageAlt: Whole short train begins rolling away from warehouse; rails curve gently ahead and all wheelsets stay on them.
pages.pageDescription: Whole short train begins rolling away from warehouse; rails curve gently ahead and all wheelsets stay on them.
pages.state: Blue/red/yellow/green sequence; no gaps at couplers.

pages.text:
The cars follow the same rails.
Their boxes travel together.
pages.imageBrief: Elevated three-quarter view of the complete train following one gentle bend; car bodies pivot naturally above bogies.
pages.imageAlt: Elevated three-quarter view of the complete train following one gentle bend; car bodies pivot naturally above bogies.
pages.pageDescription: Elevated three-quarter view of the complete train following one gentle bend; car bodies pivot naturally above bogies.
pages.state: Same three loaded closed cars; no unexplained extra vehicle.

pages.text:
The train stops by another warehouse.
Workers take the boxes out.
pages.imageBrief: At second warehouse the stopped cars have open side doors; an adult unloads a crate with appropriate pallet equipment.
pages.imageAlt: At second warehouse the stopped cars have open side doors; an adult unloads a crate with appropriate pallet equipment.
pages.pageDescription: At second warehouse the stopped cars have open side doors; an adult unloads a crate with appropriate pallet equipment.
pages.state: All cars stationary; crates decrease only through unloading.

pages.text:
One engine pulls three linked cars.
Many boxes make one trip.
pages.imageBrief: Final broad view shows blue locomotive with the three stationary cars and delivered crates neatly beside second warehouse.
pages.imageAlt: Final broad view shows blue locomotive with the three stationary cars and delivered crates neatly beside second warehouse.
pages.pageDescription: Final broad view shows blue locomotive with the three stationary cars and delivered crates neatly beside second warehouse.
pages.state: The three-car load has arrived; couplers remain connected.

oral.prompt: How did one engine move all three cars?
oral.listenFor: The couplers joined the cars, so the engine could pull them together.

visual.lookFor: The connected gray metal couplers between the car ends.

levelRationale: Candidate public B: a single visible part-to-whole mechanism and ordered journey, short present-tense sentences and repeated concrete referents. Independent calibration remains pending.

languagePrep.meaning: the powered part of this train
a strong link joining two train cars
one of the long metal strips under train wheels

title: One Ocean Around Earth

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: Do the named oceans have walls between their waters?
storyBibleReview.progression: Trace an uninterrupted water route on a globe from the Atlantic around the Southern Ocean into the Indian and Pacific, then toward the Arctic; return to the global view.
storyBibleReview.synthesis: Five names identify connected regions of one global ocean, not five separate pools.

scienceSources.title: NOAA National Ocean Service: How many oceans are there?
scienceSources.evidence: One global ocean has commonly recognized Atlantic, Pacific, Indian, Southern and Arctic regions. Boundaries are named conventions, not physical walls. The book follows the commonly used five-ocean convention.

setting: A classroom globe investigation with Kit and Zoe. Geographically accurate continent outlines on a plain globe and close map views; ocean regions stay the same blue. Route is a thin orange teaching overlay, never a real painted line on Earth.
props: Thin orange route overlay kept entirely in seawater
coverBrief: Kit traces blue water on an accurate globe while Zoe points to a second connected ocean region. No labels or political boundaries.

pages.text:
Earth has five named oceans.
Are their waters separate?
pages.imageBrief: Kit and Zoe look at the globe, Atlantic-facing. Ocean regions are uniformly blue without boundary walls.
pages.imageAlt: Kit and Zoe look at the globe, Atlantic-facing. Ocean regions are uniformly blue without boundary walls.
pages.pageDescription: Kit and Zoe look at the globe, Atlantic-facing. Ocean regions are uniformly blue without boundary walls.
pages.state: Whole globe; no route yet.

pages.text:
Start in the Atlantic Ocean.
Follow its water south.
pages.imageBrief: Accurate Atlantic-facing globe close-up with orange route from central Atlantic down past South America toward Antarctica.
pages.imageAlt: Accurate Atlantic-facing globe close-up with orange route from central Atlantic down past South America toward Antarctica.
pages.pageDescription: Accurate Atlantic-facing globe close-up with orange route from central Atlantic down past South America toward Antarctica.
pages.state: Route begins in Atlantic and stays in water.

pages.text:
The Southern Ocean circles Antarctica.
Its water meets the Atlantic.
pages.imageBrief: Polar-oblique globe view follows route through Southern Ocean around Antarctica, showing southern tip of South America behind.
pages.imageAlt: Polar-oblique globe view follows route through Southern Ocean around Antarctica, showing southern tip of South America behind.
pages.pageDescription: Polar-oblique globe view follows route through Southern Ocean around Antarctica, showing southern tip of South America behind.
pages.state: Atlantic route joins Southern Ocean; Antarctica stays solid land.

pages.text:
Go past Africa into the Indian Ocean.
There is no wall.
pages.imageBrief: Route arcs through water south of Africa and northward into Indian Ocean; Africa left, India above, Australia right.
pages.imageAlt: Route arcs through water south of Africa and northward into Indian Ocean; Africa left, India above, Australia right.
pages.pageDescription: Route arcs through water south of Africa and northward into Indian Ocean; Africa left, India above, Australia right.
pages.state: Continuous route has not crossed land.

pages.text:
Pass Australia into the Pacific Ocean.
The blue water keeps going.
pages.imageBrief: Route follows open water south of Australia into Pacific, not across Australia or through islands.
pages.imageAlt: Route follows open water south of Australia into Pacific, not across Australia or through islands.
pages.pageDescription: Route follows open water south of Australia into Pacific, not across Australia or through islands.
pages.state: The orange line continues from Indian to Pacific water.

pages.text:
A narrow sea gap leads north.
It joins the Arctic Ocean.
pages.imageBrief: Accurate northern Pacific/Bering Strait/Arctic close map with unobstructed narrow water passage between Alaska and northeast Asia.
pages.imageAlt: Accurate northern Pacific/Bering Strait/Arctic close map with unobstructed narrow water passage between Alaska and northeast Asia.
pages.pageDescription: Accurate northern Pacific/Bering Strait/Arctic close map with unobstructed narrow water passage between Alaska and northeast Asia.
pages.state: Route through Bering Strait; mainland shapes and islands accurate.

pages.text:
Five names mark different ocean regions.
Water can move between them.
pages.imageBrief: Single accurate world map integrates the completed route across named ocean regions, with no separating colored barriers.
pages.imageAlt: Single accurate world map integrates the completed route across named ocean regions, with no separating colored barriers.
pages.pageDescription: Single accurate world map integrates the completed route across named ocean regions, with no separating colored barriers.
pages.state: All five regions shown as connected blue water.
pages.embeddedImageText: Atlantic Ocean; Southern Ocean; Indian Ocean; Pacific Ocean; Arctic Ocean

pages.text:
Zoe traces the water again.
Earth has one connected ocean.
pages.imageBrief: Zoe traces the Atlantic-to-Southern part on the original globe while Kit watches; all water stays blue.
pages.imageAlt: Zoe traces the Atlantic-to-Southern part on the original globe while Kit watches; all water stays blue.
pages.pageDescription: Zoe traces the Atlantic-to-Southern part on the original globe while Kit watches; all water stays blue.
pages.state: Return to same globe with the connection understood.

oral.prompt: Why do five ocean names not mean five separate pools?
oral.listenFor: Their waters connect; the names identify different regions.

visual.prompt: Can the orange route reach this ocean without crossing land?
visual.lookFor: Yes. The route goes through water around southern Africa.

levelRationale: Candidate B: a connected spatial tracing sequence supports named vocabulary. Each page adds one adjacent region rather than unrelated ocean facts. Geographic names receive oral preparation; independent level review required.

languagePrep.meaning: the huge area of salty water on Earth
one part of a larger place
a round model of Earth

title: Teeth Have Different Jobs

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: How do front and back teeth help change one piece of food?
storyBibleReview.progression: Follow one bite of soft apple from front-tooth cutting to back-tooth grinding, then compare the tooth shapes.
storyBibleReview.synthesis: Different tooth shapes perform different parts of biting and chewing.

scienceSources.title: American Dental Association: Watch Your Mouth presentation
scienceSources.evidence: Incisors cut food; molars have broad chewing surfaces for crushing and grinding. Illustrations use an age-appropriate primary/mixed dentition model, without adult premolars added to a young child.

scienceSources.title: NIDCR: Oral Health in America
scienceSources.evidence: Teeth reduce food into smaller pieces; tongue and cheeks help move food for chewing and swallowing. No claim that teeth alone digest food.

setting: Zoe sits at a meal table with a safe thin apple slice. Scientific close-up diagrams show the relevant teeth and tongue without grotesque anatomy. No child eats while standing or running.
props: Accurate child jaw teaching diagram with front incisors and rear molars
coverBrief: Zoe holds a small apple slice at the table; a clearly separate teaching model of teeth rests beside her, not inside her face.

pages.text:
Zoe takes a bite of apple.
Which teeth touch it first?
pages.imageBrief: Zoe at meal table gently biting a thin apple slice using front teeth; plate beneath.
pages.imageAlt: Zoe at meal table gently biting a thin apple slice using front teeth; plate beneath.
pages.pageDescription: Zoe at meal table gently biting a thin apple slice using front teeth; plate beneath.
pages.state: One slice, one small bite, stable seated posture.

pages.text:
Her front teeth have thin edges.
They cut off a piece.
pages.imageBrief: Non-gory integrated close-up of front incisors closing through a small piece of apple.
pages.imageAlt: Non-gory integrated close-up of front incisors closing through a small piece of apple.
pages.pageDescription: Non-gory integrated close-up of front incisors closing through a small piece of apple.
pages.state: Front teeth cut a bite; remaining slice stays outside.

pages.text:
The piece moves inside her mouth.
Her tongue moves it back.
pages.imageBrief: Simple jaw teaching cutaway shows tongue positioning the small bite toward one side near molars; no choking or open throat imagery.
pages.imageAlt: Simple jaw teaching cutaway shows tongue positioning the small bite toward one side near molars; no choking or open throat imagery.
pages.pageDescription: Simple jaw teaching cutaway shows tongue positioning the small bite toward one side near molars; no choking or open throat imagery.
pages.state: Same bite moved toward rear chewing teeth.

pages.text:
Her back teeth have wide tops.
These teeth are called molars.
pages.imageBrief: Close-up teaching view of child molar chewing surfaces, naturally ridged rather than perfectly flat.
pages.imageAlt: Close-up teaching view of child molar chewing surfaces, naturally ridged rather than perfectly flat.
pages.pageDescription: Close-up teaching view of child molar chewing surfaces, naturally ridged rather than perfectly flat.
pages.state: Front-to-back position clear; no adult premolars.

pages.text:
The molars press the apple.
The piece breaks into smaller bits.
pages.imageBrief: Upper and lower molars meet around the softened bite with smaller pieces visible in the simplified model.
pages.imageAlt: Upper and lower molars meet around the softened bite with smaller pieces visible in the simplified model.
pages.pageDescription: Upper and lower molars meet around the softened bite with smaller pieces visible in the simplified model.
pages.state: Food becomes smaller; teeth anatomically aligned.

pages.text:
Zoe keeps chewing.
The bite becomes soft and small.
pages.imageBrief: Zoe with closed mouth chewing while the remaining apple slice rests on plate; calm natural meal scene.
pages.imageAlt: Zoe with closed mouth chewing while the remaining apple slice rests on plate; calm natural meal scene.
pages.pageDescription: Zoe with closed mouth chewing while the remaining apple slice rests on plate; calm natural meal scene.
pages.state: Bite still being chewed; no oversized mouth display.

pages.text:
Thin edges bite.
Wide tops crush and grind.
pages.imageBrief: One clear child-jaw diagram emphasizes incisors at front and molars behind with their matching small apple pieces.
pages.imageAlt: One clear child-jaw diagram emphasizes incisors at front and molars behind with their matching small apple pieces.
pages.pageDescription: One clear child-jaw diagram emphasizes incisors at front and molars behind with their matching small apple pieces.
pages.state: Single anatomical model compares two tooth functions.

pages.text:
Zoe swallows the small soft mouthful.
Both tooth shapes help.
pages.imageBrief: Zoe after swallowing, hands resting by plate with the remaining apple slice; same meal setting.
pages.imageAlt: Zoe after swallowing, hands resting by plate with the remaining apple slice; same meal setting.
pages.pageDescription: Zoe after swallowing, hands resting by plate with the remaining apple slice; same meal setting.
pages.state: First mouthful finished; remaining slice still has one missing bite.

oral.prompt: What did the front teeth do before the back teeth worked?
oral.listenFor: They cut off a bite; the back teeth crushed and ground it smaller.

visual.prompt: How are these back teeth different from thin front teeth?
visual.lookFor: The molars have wider chewing tops.

levelRationale: Candidate B: one familiar bite gives an ordered sequence, with two contrasting shapes and functions. Anatomy nouns are pictured and explained; no advice or generalized digestion survey.

languagePrep.meaning: a wide tooth near the back of your mouth
use your teeth to break food into smaller pieces
the thin outside part of something

title: The Windsock Turns

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: What can a windsock show when the wind changes?
storyBibleReview.progression: Observe the same windsock in calm, a steady breeze, a stronger breeze and a changed direction, then calm again.
storyBibleReview.synthesis: The windsock moves with air; its tail direction and extension give clues to the wind.

scienceSources.title: Federal Aviation Administration: Specification for Wind Cone Assemblies
scienceSources.evidence: A wind cone responds to direction and wind speed; the larger opening faces incoming air and the smaller tail extends downwind. No exact speed is inferred from this illustrative windsock.

setting: A school weather corner in an open field, not an active runway. Orange tapered fabric windsock on a freely swiveling ring atop a gray pole; blue bench permanently left of pole and green tree right.
props: Orange windsock open at both ends
coverBrief: Orange windsock extends rightward from its pole in an open school field; blue bench left and tree right remain visible.

pages.text:
The orange windsock hangs down.
The air is still.
pages.imageBrief: Same orange cone hangs limply below ring beside gray pole; blue bench left and tree right.
pages.imageAlt: Same orange cone hangs limply below ring beside gray pole; blue bench left and tree right.
pages.pageDescription: Same orange cone hangs limply below ring beside gray pole; blue bench left and tree right.
pages.state: Calm air; no moving leaves.

pages.text:
A breeze blows into its wide opening.
The cloth begins to lift.
pages.imageBrief: Air from left inflates wide opening slightly; fabric lifts toward right while tail still droops.
pages.imageAlt: Air from left inflates wide opening slightly; fabric lifts toward right while tail still droops.
pages.pageDescription: Air from left inflates wide opening slightly; fabric lifts toward right while tail still droops.
pages.state: Same wide opening faces left; tail lifts right.

pages.text:
Air moves through the windsock.
Its narrow tail points toward the tree.
pages.imageBrief: Cone extends toward right-hand tree with both openings physically present.
pages.imageAlt: Cone extends toward right-hand tree with both openings physically present.
pages.pageDescription: Cone extends toward right-hand tree with both openings physically present.
pages.state: Left-to-right air; no reversed airflow.

pages.text:
The wind grows stronger.
More of the windsock stretches out.
pages.imageBrief: Same cone more nearly horizontal to right; green tree leaves lean slightly right.
pages.imageAlt: Same cone more nearly horizontal to right; green tree leaves lean slightly right.
pages.pageDescription: Same cone more nearly horizontal to right; green tree leaves lean slightly right.
pages.state: Stronger breeze, same direction; no numerical speed claim.

pages.text:
Now the wind changes direction.
The windsock swings around the pole.
pages.imageBrief: Cone has swung through a clear oblique intermediate angle on free ring; pole stationary.
pages.imageAlt: Cone has swung through a clear oblique intermediate angle on free ring; pole stationary.
pages.pageDescription: Cone has swung through a clear oblique intermediate angle on free ring; pole stationary.
pages.state: Transition from rightward to leftward flow.

pages.text:
Its tail points toward the bench.
The air now blows that way.
pages.imageBrief: Cone fully extends left toward blue bench; wide opening on right faces incoming air.
pages.imageAlt: Cone fully extends left toward blue bench; wide opening on right faces incoming air.
pages.pageDescription: Cone fully extends left toward blue bench; wide opening on right faces incoming air.
pages.state: Right-to-left air; tree and bench have not swapped places.

pages.text:
The wind stops.
The cloth hangs beside the pole again.
pages.imageBrief: Cone droops limply beside same pole; background leaves still.
pages.imageAlt: Cone droops limply beside same pole; background leaves still.
pages.pageDescription: Cone droops limply beside same pole; background leaves still.
pages.state: Return to calm after changed-direction breeze.

pages.text:
We cannot see the air.
The moving windsock shows its direction.
pages.imageBrief: A new gentle left-to-right breeze lifts cone partly toward tree; show no fantasy visible wind ribbons.
pages.imageAlt: A new gentle left-to-right breeze lifts cone partly toward tree; show no fantasy visible wind ribbons.
pages.pageDescription: A new gentle left-to-right breeze lifts cone partly toward tree; show no fantasy visible wind ribbons.
pages.state: Observed cloth movement is evidence of unseen air movement.

oral.prompt: What made the tail point toward a different place?
oral.listenFor: The wind changed direction and turned the windsock.

visual.prompt: Which place is the air moving toward now?
visual.lookFor: Toward the blue bench, in the same direction as the narrow tail.

levelRationale: Candidate B: repeated visible state changes around two fixed landmarks support one observational relationship. No compass points, knots or abstract weather systems are required.

languagePrep.meaning: a cloth tube that moves with the wind
a light wind
the way something moves or points

title: A Mirror Moves the Light

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: Can turning a mirror move a bright spot without moving the flashlight?
storyBibleReview.progression: Establish a fixed flashlight, mirror and reflected spot; rotate only the mirror, compare moved spot, block the light and restore it.
storyBibleReview.synthesis: A mirror reflects light in a different direction; changing the mirror changes where the light lands.

scienceSources.title: University of Waikato Science Learning Hub: Reflection of light
scienceSources.evidence: Light reflects from a smooth surface, with reflection angle determined by the surface angle. The flashlight remains fixed; the mirror is moved, not the source. Ordinary clear air does not show a solid beam.

setting: Dim classroom demonstration on a low table. Low-power flashlight fixed in a wooden cradle, small shatterproof plane mirror in a turning stand, white vertical screen on the right. No lasers, sunlight or light aimed into eyes.
props: One yellow flashlight held stationary in cradle
One plane mirror in gray stand
coverBrief: Kit gently turns the small mirror and Zoe points to a bright spot on the white screen. Flashlight sits untouched in its cradle.

pages.text:
The flashlight shines at a small mirror.
A bright spot reaches the screen.
pages.imageBrief: Establish fixed flashlight aiming diagonally onto mirror; mirror reflects toward white screen with one bright spot.
pages.imageAlt: Establish fixed flashlight aiming diagonally onto mirror; mirror reflects toward white screen with one bright spot.
pages.pageDescription: Establish fixed flashlight aiming diagonally onto mirror; mirror reflects toward white screen with one bright spot.
pages.state: Flashlight and screen fixed; mirror at starting angle.

pages.text:
Light hits the mirror.
The mirror sends it another way.
pages.imageBrief: One integrated top-view diagram shows only two thin yellow teaching arrows: source to mirror, mirror to screen.
pages.imageAlt: One integrated top-view diagram shows only two thin yellow teaching arrows: source to mirror, mirror to screen.
pages.pageDescription: One integrated top-view diagram shows only two thin yellow teaching arrows: source to mirror, mirror to screen.
pages.state: Equal incidence/reflection geometry, no extra beam.

pages.text:
Kit turns only the mirror.
The flashlight stays in its stand.
pages.imageBrief: Kit holds mirror stand safely and changes its angle; both flashlight and screen remain fixed.
pages.imageAlt: Kit holds mirror stand safely and changes its angle; both flashlight and screen remain fixed.
pages.pageDescription: Kit holds mirror stand safely and changes its angle; both flashlight and screen remain fixed.
pages.state: Mirror angle changed; other props unmoved.

pages.text:
The bright spot moves across the screen.
Zoe follows it with her finger.
pages.imageBrief: New spot lies farther right on same screen; Zoe points below it without touching or blocking mirror.
pages.imageAlt: New spot lies farther right on same screen; Zoe points below it without touching or blocking mirror.
pages.pageDescription: New spot lies farther right on same screen; Zoe points below it without touching or blocking mirror.
pages.state: New mirror angle and spot location agree.

pages.text:
Zoe holds a card before the mirror.
The bright spot disappears.
pages.imageBrief: Opaque blue card intercepts flashlight light before mirror; flashlight spot now on card and screen dark.
pages.imageAlt: Opaque blue card intercepts flashlight light before mirror; flashlight spot now on card and screen dark.
pages.pageDescription: Opaque blue card intercepts flashlight light before mirror; flashlight spot now on card and screen dark.
pages.state: Light blocked before mirror; source still on.

pages.text:
She lifts the card away.
The bright spot returns.
pages.imageBrief: Card raised clear of optical path; reflected spot returns to page4 screen position.
pages.imageAlt: Card raised clear of optical path; reflected spot returns to page4 screen position.
pages.pageDescription: Card raised clear of optical path; reflected spot returns to page4 screen position.
pages.state: Same angle and returned light path.

pages.text:
Kit turns the mirror back.
The spot returns to its first place.
pages.imageBrief: Mirror restored to original orientation; spot in original page1 position.
pages.imageAlt: Mirror restored to original orientation; spot in original page1 position.
pages.pageDescription: Mirror restored to original orientation; spot in original page1 position.
pages.state: Controlled reversal with source and screen unchanged.

pages.text:
The flashlight stays still.
Turning the mirror changes the light’s path.
pages.imageBrief: Final single scene includes fixed flashlight, original mirror angle and screen spot; children observe the route.
pages.imageAlt: Final single scene includes fixed flashlight, original mirror angle and screen spot; children observe the route.
pages.pageDescription: Final single scene includes fixed flashlight, original mirror angle and screen spot; children observe the route.
pages.state: Inquiry closed by changed reflector with fixed source.

oral.prompt: What moved the bright spot while the flashlight stayed still?
oral.listenFor: Turning the mirror changed the direction of reflected light.

visual.prompt: Why is the white screen dark here?
visual.lookFor: The blue card stops the flashlight’s light before it reaches the mirror.

levelRationale: Candidate B: a controlled visible change, short sentences and repeated props support cause and comparison. Diagram arrows are declared teaching marks, not visible light ropes.

languagePrep.meaning: a smooth surface that sends back light
send light back from a surface
the route something follows

title: The Camera Keeps a Picture

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: What stays in a photograph after the real scene changes?
storyBibleReview.progression: Frame one red block on a blue block, record the view, rearrange the blocks and compare the unchanged saved photograph with the new scene.
storyBibleReview.synthesis: A saved photograph records the earlier view rather than changing with the objects.

scienceSources.title: National Science and Media Museum: Waterdrop Photography
scienceSources.evidence: A camera records light entering through its lens at a particular moment. This book distinguishes a saved photograph from a live preview.

scienceSources.title: Canon: RAW Image Fundamentals
scienceSources.evidence: Sensor signals are processed into an image that can be written to camera memory; recorded images retain captured scene information.

setting: Kit and Zoe at a plain table using a simple unbranded digital camera. A red cube rests on one blue rectangular block. Camera playback always has a plain triangular playback icon, with no unreadable menus.
props: Small gray digital camera with screen
coverBrief: Zoe holds a camera showing the red cube on the blue block; on the real table the red cube now sits beside the blue block. Exact intentional difference is clear.

pages.text:
A red cube rests on a blue block.
Zoe points the camera.
pages.imageBrief: Real red cube centered atop blue block; Zoe aims camera lens at them, Kit watches.
pages.imageAlt: Real red cube centered atop blue block; Zoe aims camera lens at them, Kit watches.
pages.pageDescription: Real red cube centered atop blue block; Zoe aims camera lens at them, Kit watches.
pages.state: Original stacked arrangement, no saved image shown yet.

pages.text:
Light enters the camera through its lens.
Zoe can see the blocks.
pages.imageBrief: Over-shoulder camera view shows live preview matching stacked blocks exactly.
pages.imageAlt: Over-shoulder camera view shows live preview matching stacked blocks exactly.
pages.pageDescription: Over-shoulder camera view shows live preview matching stacked blocks exactly.
pages.state: Lens faces real blocks; preview same orientation.

pages.text:
Zoe presses the button.
The camera saves a picture.
pages.imageBrief: Finger presses top shutter button with correct grip; actual blocks untouched.
pages.imageAlt: Finger presses top shutter button with correct grip; actual blocks untouched.
pages.pageDescription: Finger presses top shutter button with correct grip; actual blocks untouched.
pages.state: Photograph captured with red cube atop blue block.

pages.text:
Now Kit moves the red cube.
He sets it beside the blue block.
pages.imageBrief: Kit places red cube directly right of blue block; Zoe lowers camera.
pages.imageAlt: Kit places red cube directly right of blue block; Zoe lowers camera.
pages.pageDescription: Kit places red cube directly right of blue block; Zoe lowers camera.
pages.state: Real blocks side by side; saved photograph remains stacked.

pages.text:
Zoe opens the saved picture.
The red cube still sits on top.
pages.imageBrief: Close camera playback display with triangular icon shows original stacked arrangement.
pages.imageAlt: Close camera playback display with triangular icon shows original stacked arrangement.
pages.pageDescription: Close camera playback display with triangular icon shows original stacked arrangement.
pages.state: Display explicitly saved playback, not live preview.

pages.text:
Kit checks the real blocks.
The red cube sits beside the blue block.
pages.imageBrief: Kit compares real red cube right of the single blue block with saved stacked image held by Zoe.
pages.imageAlt: Kit compares real red cube right of the single blue block with saved stacked image held by Zoe.
pages.pageDescription: Kit compares real red cube right of the single blue block with saved stacked image held by Zoe.
pages.state: Exactly two real objects; plural blocks refers to arrangement, no extra props.

pages.text:
The red cube is beside the block.
The saved picture stays the same.
pages.imageBrief: Same real side-by-side objects and saved stacked display in one coherent over-shoulder scene.
pages.imageAlt: Same real side-by-side objects and saved stacked display in one coherent over-shoulder scene.
pages.pageDescription: Same real side-by-side objects and saved stacked display in one coherent over-shoulder scene.
pages.state: Intentional before/current comparison retained.

pages.text:
The photo shows the earlier view.
It keeps the red cube on top.

title: Milk into Cheese

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: How can liquid milk become this soft fresh cheese?

storyBibleReview.synthesis: The solid curds stay in the cloth while liquid whey drains away, producing this fresh cheese.

scienceSources.title: Oregon State University Extension: Cheeses of the World
scienceSources.evidence: Describes heated milk plus lemon juice forming curds, with liquid whey separated by draining. This is one acid-set fresh cheese, not the method for all cheeses.

scienceSources.title: Oregon State University Extension: The basics of cheesemaking
scienceSources.evidence: Start with pasteurized milk and sanitized equipment. Book is an observed process, not an unsupervised recipe or food-storage instruction.

This soft cheese begins as milk.

pages.imageAlt: Clear integrated close view of pan contents shows solid white curds in pale yellowish whey.

pages.pageDescription: Close view of pale whey dripping from supported cloth into glass bowl.

pages.imageAlt: Drained white curds form a soft mound inside open cloth; substantial whey remains in bowl.
pages.pageDescription: Drained white curds form a soft mound inside open cloth; substantial whey remains in bowl.

The cloth holds the cheese.

pages.imageAlt: Final intact draining setup displays the two outcomes, white curds above and pale liquid below.
pages.pageDescription: Final intact draining setup displays the two outcomes, white curds above and pale liquid below.

title: A Giraffe Reaches Up

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: How does this giraffe get leaves from a thorny tree?
storyBibleReview.progression: Follow one feeding reach from locating leaves to reaching, wrapping the tongue, pulling leaves and chewing while thorns remain on the twig.
storyBibleReview.synthesis: Height brings the mouth near the leaves; a long flexible tongue helps collect them between thorns.

scienceSources.title: Giraffe Conservation Foundation: What do giraffe eat?
scienceSources.evidence: Giraffes browse leaves/shoots; long muscular tongues help select leaves among thorns. This book follows one natural example rather than claiming all food is high or all thorns are avoided.

scienceSources.title: Giraffe Conservation Foundation: How long is a giraffe’s tongue?
scienceSources.evidence: A flexible prehensile tongue works with lips to grasp foliage. Dark tongue coloration and anatomically plausible reach should be retained.

setting: One wild southern giraffe browsing a Vachellia tree in open African woodland. Natural anatomy, four legs, two ossicones, short mane, dark tongue, consistent tan coat and irregular brown patches. No named or speaking animals.

One target leafy branch within natural reach
coverBrief: Giraffe reaches toward a leafy thorn branch; long dark tongue curls around foliage while distinct thorns remain on the twig.

pages.pageDescription: Close profile of accurate muzzle and dark flexible tongue curling among leaflets.

pages.pageDescription: Tongue and lips grasp leaflets while woody thorn-bearing twig stays outside.

pages.pageDescription: Final close feeding reach combines neck height and grasping tongue in one coherent scene.

title: No Gaps in the Line

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: Why must equal cubes touch when we measure a book’s width?
storyBibleReview.progression: Compare a gapped line of five equal cubes with an end-to-end line, fill the exposed space with a sixth cube and read the corrected width.
storyBibleReview.synthesis: Equal units must cover the whole length with no gaps or overlaps; this model book is six cubes wide.

scienceSources.title: National Centre for Excellence in the Teaching of Mathematics: Measures
scienceSources.evidence: Repeated equal-size units measure length accurately only with complete coverage, no gaps or overlaps. The six-cube width is an explicit illustrative model, not a universal book dimension.

setting: Kit and Zoe measure a plain blue book on a white table. Book width exactly six unit cubes. Six identical yellow cubes; no numerals on cubes. View remains top-oblique with book bottom edge horizontal.
props: Plain blue book exactly six cubes wide
Exactly six equal yellow unit cubes

title: Saturn’s Rings Are Pieces

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: Are Saturn’s rings one solid sheet?
storyBibleReview.progression: Move from a whole-planet ring view to a clearly declared imagined close view of separate particles, observe gaps and circling motion, then return to the distant view.
storyBibleReview.synthesis: Countless separate mostly icy pieces look like smooth rings from far away.

scienceSources.title: NASA Cassini: FAQ
scienceSources.evidence: Rings are separate water-ice particles mixed with dust and rock fragments, with each particle orbiting Saturn. No astronauts or direct child visit are implied.

scienceSources.title: NASA Cassini: Rings
scienceSources.evidence: The rings consist predominantly of many ice pieces of different sizes. Illustrations distinguish a distant view from an explanatory close view, not actual telescope resolution.

setting: Scientific illustration journey around Saturn. No children or spacecraft visiting. Pale gold gas planet with restrained flat bands; rings in its equatorial plane. Close particle views are explicitly illustrations, not photographs.
props: Saturn with accurately oriented flat equatorial rings
Many separate irregular pale icy particles
Space background without dense decorative stars
coverBrief: Saturn and flat rings in three-quarter view, with a small integrated magnified area showing separate icy pieces. No labels or fantasy ring road.

pages.text:
Wide rings circle Saturn.

pages.imageBrief: Whole Saturn with flat bright rings crossing in front and hidden behind the planet correctly.
pages.imageAlt: Whole Saturn with flat bright rings crossing in front and hidden behind the planet correctly.
pages.pageDescription: Whole Saturn with flat bright rings crossing in front and hidden behind the planet correctly.
pages.state: Distant view makes rings appear continuous.

pages.imageAlt: Integrated close scientific view of many irregular pale icy particles separated by black space, not joined tiles.
pages.pageDescription: Integrated close scientific view of many irregular pale icy particles separated by black space, not joined tiles.
pages.state: Imagined microscopic-scale relative view; no solid sheet.

pages.pageDescription: Closer clear view emphasizes gaps between separate irregular ice particles.

pages.pageDescription: Wider ring-section diagram shows three small consistent curved direction arrows tangent to particle orbits, planet interior to curves.
pages.state: All main-ring particles move around Saturn rather than one spinning sheet.

pages.imageAlt: Return outward to complete planet and rings; individual chunks no longer resolvable.
pages.pageDescription: Return outward to complete planet and rings; individual chunks no longer resolvable.
pages.state: Visual blending from distance, not physical fusion.

The rings look smooth from far away.

pages.imageAlt: One integrated comparison illustration connects wide Saturn view to magnified particle area with a clear zoom connector.
pages.pageDescription: One integrated comparison illustration connects wide Saturn view to magnified particle area with a clear zoom connector.
